text: Provable, not visible. This is how the attested market is built.
It starts with one decision. The chain is a notary and a settlement rail, not a database.
On chain goes only what must be verified later, without trusting us: commitments, identities, grants, signatures, settlement state, and the audit log root.
Anything someone needs to read stays off chain: records, mandates, the matching engine, models, documents. And keys never leave a hardware security module.
Around that ledger sit eight services. Identity, ingestion, the record store, attestation. Matching, settlement, the agent runtime, and integration.
Every service writes commitments to the ledger, and reads grants from it. None of them stores state there.
Now, follow one record. A rent roll leaves the owner's property system through an adapter. Ingestion extracts its fields, with lineage back to the source.
The record store encrypts each field under its own key, in the owner's vault.
Each field is hashed with a random salt, because N-O-I equals eight hundred thousand is guessable. An unsalted hash is a leak.
The hashes roll up into a single Merkle root, per asset, per period.
Attestation collects signatures from independent sources of the fact, computes the quorum and a level, and commits.
What reaches the chain is the root, the signatures and the level. The rent roll itself never does.
Two quorums, kept apart. Consensus orders: validators agree what happened, and when. Attestation verifies: independent sources sign that a fact is true enough to act on.
The validators are named parties, like notaries, auditors and banks, anchored to a public chain that no consortium member controls.
A buyer's agent gets a grant: the value and salt for named fields only. It checks them against the root on chain, and the grant itself is logged.
Where the double-blind market needs it, a range proof answers: is N-O-I at least X? Without revealing it.
Every action traces to a person: institution, principal, agent credential, action. Agents prepare. Anything that binds also carries a principal's signature.
Matching runs deterministically in an attested enclave, with roots in and a root out. Neutrality becomes verifiable.
List, diligence, match, finance, settle. Each step leaves a mark on chain a regulator can verify, without seeing a rent, a mandate or a price. And operate repeats it, monthly.
None of this asks an intermediary to change their systems. First, shadow: adapters read what exists. Then, write back, in their own format. Then, they work on the platform, because it's faster.
Every adapter is one untrusted source. A compromised adapter can lie. It cannot reach a quorum alone.
A bank gets three connectors: its financing pack in, its credit policy out, and a servicing feed. Neither bank system is replaced.
Safety starts with a split. A data breach costs confidentiality; a key compromise is money gone. So data and value sit on different keys, networks and teams.
And assume a key will be compromised. Alone, it can do nothing. With a second, only a little. And with a third, it can be reversed.
Commit first. Connect second. Match third. Settle last.
